content: 1. GIAZO is a locally acting aminosalicylate approved for treating mild to moderately active ulcerative colitis in male patients aged 18 years and older. Its effectiveness in female patients was not demonstrated in clinical trials. The safety and efficacy of GIAZO in children under 18 years of age have not been established. 2. COLAZAL is another aminosalicylate, but its safety and effectiveness in adults beyond 12 weeks of use have not been established. Similarly, in pediatric patients aged 5 to 17 years, its safety and efficacy beyond 8 weeks remain unproven. 3. Balsalazide can increase the levels or effects of baricitinib by reducing its elimination. Co-administration with strong organic anion transporter 3 (OAT3) inhibitors is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be considered. 4. Balsalazide may interact with live vaccines such as measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccines, increasing the risk of Reye's syndrome. Salicylate use should be avoided for six weeks following vaccination. 5. Co-administration of acetazolamide and balsalazide can lead to increased plasma levels of both drugs due to inhibition of renal tubular secretion. This interaction may also increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Azithromycin can decrease the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Brinzolamide and balsalazide may increase each other's plasma levels due to inhibition of renal tubular secretion. This interaction may also lead to potential neurotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Clarithromycin and other antibiotics, such as erythromycin (in various forms), can reduce the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Griseofulvin decreases balsalazide levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Methazolamide and balsalazide may increase each other's plasma levels due to inhibition of renal tubular secretion, potentially leading to neurotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Balsalazide can increase the levels or effects of mycophenolate and probenecid by competing for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Roxithromycin and other antibiotics, such as temocillin, can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Balsalazide may increase the effects of warfarin by enhancing anticoagulation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, diclofenac, and naproxen can increase balsalazide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Balsalazide can increase the effects of insulin (various types) through pharmacodynamic synergy, particularly at high salicylate doses. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, and metronidazole can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Balsalazide can decrease the levels of folic acid and cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Alcohol (ethanol) may increase the toxicity of balsalazide through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Willow bark, which contains salicylic acid, may have additive effects or toxicity when combined with balsalazide. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Calcium carbonate and other agents that increase urinary pH can alter the renal reabsorption of salicylates, leading to increased salicylate levels at moderate doses and decreased levels at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion. 21. Live vaccines such as varicella virus vaccine should be avoided in patients taking balsalazide due to the risk of Reye's syndrome. Salicylate use should be avoided for six weeks after vaccination. 22. Verapamil may enhance the antiplatelet activity of balsalazide through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Sodium bicarbonate and other alkalinizing agents can increase salicylate levels at moderate doses and decrease them at high doses due to changes in renal excretion. 24. Antibiotics such as vancomycin, tetracycline, and linezolid can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. NSAIDs such as ketoprofen, indomethacin, and meloxicam can increase balsalazide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Balsalazide can increase the levels or effects of mesalamine by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Corticosteroids such as prednisone and dexamethasone can decrease balsalazide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Trimethoprim and other antibiotics can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Balsalazide can increase the levels or effects of valacyclovir and ganciclovir by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Sulfonamides such as sulfamethoxazole and sulfisoxazole can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. Balsalazide may also increase sulfonamide levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 31. Tobramycin and other aminoglycosides can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Salsalate and other salicylates can increase balsalazide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Fleroxacin and other fluoroquinolones can reduce balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Methyclothiazide and other diuretics can increase balsalazide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Mefenamic acid and other NSAIDs can increase balsalazide levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Rose hips can increase balsalazide levels by reducing renal clearance. Conversely, balsalazide can decrease rose hips levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions and considerations for balsalazide and related agents.
